summaryEn: A conference on "Aerial Phenomena" was held 16 February 1949 at 1300 in conference room P-162, Los Alamos Scientific Laboratory. The subject was classified Secret under AR 380-5 and attendees were properly cleared; participants included 4th Army officers, Dr. LaPaz (University of Nevada), FBI, USAEC representatives, and University of California scientists (Dr. Bradbury, Dr. Holloway, Mr. Hoyt, Dr. Menley, Dr. Reines, Dr. Teller). Captain Beet reviewed reports beginning in December 1948 from airline pilots and introduced Dr. LaPaz, who contrasted conventional meteorite falls with observed incidents. Dr. LaPaz described the so-called Starvation Peak incident (date given as December 12 in the text, original has uncertain notation) as appearing instantly at full intensity, color estimated near 5200 Å (green to yellow-green), following an approximately horizontal trajectory at roughly constant angular velocity, fragmenting near the end while remaining bright, and lasting about two seconds. He reported using a stopwatch and a transit to obtain azimuth and elevation measurements and noted that a complete file of reports exists; portions of the record were obscured by external noise.
